text: Find the determinant of the matrix \(\begin{pmatrix} 9 & -4 \\ 2 & -7 \end{pmatrix}\).
explanation:

Top row: \(-4 + (5) = 1\), \(3 + (5) = 8\)

Bottom row: \(-3 + (3) = 0\), \(0 + (-2) = -2\)

So \(A + B = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 8 \\ 0 & -2 \end{pmatrix}\).

text: Find the inverse of the matrix \(\begin{pmatrix} 5 & 4 \\ 1 & 4 \end{pmatrix}\).

Bottom row: \(4 + (-4) = 0\), \(-3 + (6) = 3\)

So \(A + B = \begin{pmatrix} 6 & 14 \\ 0 & 3 \end{pmatrix}\).

Top-right: \((-1)(-3) + (3)(-3) = -6\)

Bottom-left: \((-1)(-2) + (1)(2) = 4\)

Bottom-right: \((-1)(-3) + (1)(-3) = 0\)

So \(AB = \begin{pmatrix} 8 & -6 \\ 4 & 0 \end{pmatrix}\).

Top row: \(9 + (4) = 13\), \(9 + (9) = 18\)

Bottom row: \(-6 + (4) = -2\), \(-5 + (-6) = -11\)

So \(A + B = \begin{pmatrix} 13 & 18 \\ -2 & -11 \end{pmatrix}\).

Multiply every element of the matrix by 6.

Add the matrices element by element.

Top row: \(3 + (5) = 8\), \(-3 + (-1) = -4\)

Bottom row: \(7 + (-1) = 6\), \(3 + (-1) = 2\)

So \(A + B = \begin{pmatrix} 8 & -4 \\ 6 & 2 \end{pmatrix}\).

For \(\begin{pmatrix} a & b \\ c & d \end{pmatrix}\), the inverse is \(\frac{1}{ad-bc}\begin{pmatrix} d & -b \\ -c & a \end{pmatrix}\).

Determinant \(= (4)(3) - (1)(6) = 6\)

So the inverse is \(\frac{1}{6}\begin{pmatrix} 3 & -1 \\ -6 & 4 \end{pmatrix}\).

Add the matrices element by element.

Top row: \(-4 + (-5) = -9\), \(-7 + (2) = -5\)

Bottom row: \(-4 + (3) = -1\), \(7 + (1) = 8\)

So \(A + B = \begin{pmatrix} -9 & -5 \\ -1 & 8 \end{pmatrix}\).

text: Find the determinant of the matrix \(\begin{pmatrix} -8 & 4 \\ -5 & -6 \end{pmatrix}\).
explanation:
For \(\begin{pmatrix} a & b \\ c & d \end{pmatrix}\), the determinant is \(ad - bc\).

\(= (-8)(-6) - (4)(-5)\)

\(= 48 - -20 = 68\)

text: Find the inverse of the matrix \(\begin{pmatrix} 2 & 5 \\ 2 & 6 \end{pmatrix}\).
explanation:
For \(\begin{pmatrix} a & b \\ c & d \end{pmatrix}\), the inverse is \(\frac{1}{ad-bc}\begin{pmatrix} d & -b \\ -c & a \end{pmatrix}\).

Determinant \(= (2)(6) - (5)(2) = 2\)

So the inverse is \(\frac{1}{2}\begin{pmatrix} 6 & -5 \\ -2 & 2 \end{pmatrix}\).

Add the matrices element by element.

Top row: \(5 + (-4) = 1\), \(6 + (0) = 6\)

Bottom row: \(6 + (2) = 8\), \(8 + (6) = 14\)

So \(A + B = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 6 \\ 8 & 14 \end{pmatrix}\).

Add the matrices element by element.

Top row: \(0 + (-6) = -6\), \(-6 + (-4) = -10\)

Bottom row: \(4 + (-6) = -2\), \(8 + (-1) = 7\)

So \(A + B = \begin{pmatrix} -6 & -10 \\ -2 & 7 \end{pmatrix}\).

Multiply row by column.

Top-left: \((5)(5) + (2)(0) = 25\)

Top-right: \((5)(1) + (2)(5) = 15\)

Bottom-left: \((-3)(5) + (5)(0) = -15\)

Bottom-right: \((-3)(1) + (5)(5) = 22\)

So \(AB = \begin{pmatrix} 25 & 15 \\ -15 & 22 \end{pmatrix}\).

Add the matrices element by element.

Top row: \(-4 + (9) = 5\), \(8 + (3) = 11\)

Bottom row: \(-7 + (8) = 1\), \(1 + (8) = 9\)

So \(A + B = \begin{pmatrix} 5 & 11 \\ 1 & 9 \end{pmatrix}\).

text: Find the inverse of the matrix \(\begin{pmatrix} 5 & 5 \\ 2 & 3 \end{pmatrix}\).
explanation:
For \(\begin{pmatrix} a & b \\ c & d \end{pmatrix}\), the inverse is \(\frac{1}{ad-bc}\begin{pmatrix} d & -b \\ -c & a \end{pmatrix}\).

Determinant \(= (5)(3) - (5)(2) = 5\)

So the inverse is \(\frac{1}{5}\begin{pmatrix} 3 & -5 \\ -2 & 5 \end{pmatrix}\).

Multiply every element of the matrix by 3.

\(3A = \begin{pmatrix} 0 & -3 \\ -6 & -12 \end{pmatrix}\)

text: Find the determinant of the matrix \(\begin{pmatrix} -4 & 4 \\ 3 & -2 \end{pmatrix}\).
explanation:
For \(\begin{pmatrix} a & b \\ c & d \end{pmatrix}\), the determinant is \(ad - bc\).

\(= (-4)(-2) - (4)(3)\)

\(= 8 - 12 = -4\)

Add the matrices element by element.

Top row: \(6 + (-1) = 5\), \(8 + (2) = 10\)

Bottom row: \(5 + (-1) = 4\), \(8 + (4) = 12\)

So \(A + B = \begin{pmatrix} 5 & 10 \\ 4 & 12 \end{pmatrix}\).

Add the matrices element by element.

Top row: \(9 + (6) = 15\), \(-5 + (-1) = -6\)

Bottom row: \(9 + (8) = 17\), \(0 + (3) = 3\)

So \(A + B = \begin{pmatrix} 15 & -6 \\ 17 & 3 \end{pmatrix}\).

text: Find the inverse of the matrix \(\begin{pmatrix} 3 & 4 \\ 3 & 6 \end{pmatrix}\).
explanation:
For \(\begin{pmatrix} a & b \\ c & d \end{pmatrix}\), the inverse is \(\frac{1}{ad-bc}\begin{pmatrix} d & -b \\ -c & a \end{pmatrix}\).

Determinant \(= (3)(6) - (4)(3) = 6\)

So the inverse is \(\frac{1}{6}\begin{pmatrix} 6 & -4 \\ -3 & 3 \end{pmatrix}\).

Multiply every element of the matrix by 3.

\(3A = \begin{pmatrix} -18 & -15 \\ -9 & -9 \end{pmatrix}\)

Add the matrices element by element.

Top row: \(4 + (3) = 7\), \(9 + (3) = 12\)

Bottom row: \(1 + (-6) = -5\), \(-2 + (4) = 2\)

So \(A + B = \begin{pmatrix} 7 & 12 \\ -5 & 2 \end{pmatrix}\).

text: Find the value of \(x\) for which the matrix \(\begin{pmatrix} x & 6 \\ 3 & 3 \end{pmatrix}\) has no inverse.
explanation:
A matrix has no inverse when its determinant is zero.

\(\det = (x)(3) - (6)(3) = 3x - 18\)

Setting \(3x - 18 = 0\): \(x = \frac{18}{3} = 6\)

text: Find the determinant of the matrix \(\begin{pmatrix} 7 & 8 \\ 9 & 4 \end{pmatrix}\).
explanation:
For \(\begin{pmatrix} a & b \\ c & d \end{pmatrix}\), the determinant is \(ad - bc\).

\(= (7)(4) - (8)(9)\)

\(= 28 - 72 = -44\)

Multiply every element of the matrix by 6.

\(6A = \begin{pmatrix} -36 & 12 \\ -24 & -12 \end{pmatrix}\)

text: Find the inverse of the matrix \(\begin{pmatrix} 6 & 4 \\ 4 & 4 \end{pmatrix}\).
explanation:
For \(\begin{pmatrix} a & b \\ c & d \end{pmatrix}\), the inverse is \(\frac{1}{ad-bc}\begin{pmatrix} d & -b \\ -c & a \end{pmatrix}\).

Determinant \(= (6)(4) - (4)(4) = 8\)

So the inverse is \(\frac{1}{8}\begin{pmatrix} 4 & -4 \\ -4 & 6 \end{pmatrix}\).

Multiply row by column.

Top-left: \((3)(3) + (1)(2) = 11\)

Top-right: \((3)(3) + (1)(-3) = 6\)

Bottom-left: \((4)(3) + (5)(2) = 22\)

Bottom-right: \((4)(3) + (5)(-3) = -3\)

So \(AB = \begin{pmatrix} 11 & 6 \\ 22 & -3 \end{pmatrix}\).

Add the matrices element by element.

Top row: \(-6 + (2) = -4\), \(5 + (7) = 12\)

Bottom row: \(7 + (2) = 9\), \(7 + (5) = 12\)

So \(A + B = \begin{pmatrix} -4 & 12 \\ 9 & 12 \end{pmatrix}\).

Add the matrices element by element.

Top row: \(9 + (1) = 10\), \(9 + (-7) = 2\)

Bottom row: \(0 + (-2) = -2\), \(7 + (7) = 14\)

So \(A + B = \begin{pmatrix} 10 & 2 \\ -2 & 14 \end{pmatrix}\).

text: Find the determinant of the matrix \(\begin{pmatrix} 8 & -5 \\ -4 & 3 \end{pmatrix}\).
explanation:
For \(\begin{pmatrix} a & b \\ c & d \end{pmatrix}\), the determinant is \(ad - bc\).

\(= (8)(3) - (-5)(-4)\)

\(= 24 - 20 = 4\)

Add the matrices element by element.

Top row: \(-5 + (2) = -3\), \(1 + (-1) = 0\)

Bottom row: \(-7 + (1) = -6\), \(3 + (-7) = -4\)

So \(A + B = \begin{pmatrix} -3 & 0 \\ -6 & -4 \end{pmatrix}\).

Add the matrices element by element.

Top row: \(-1 + (6) = 5\), \(8 + (-1) = 7\)

Bottom row: \(-6 + (0) = -6\), \(6 + (4) = 10\)

So \(A + B = \begin{pmatrix} 5 & 7 \\ -6 & 10 \end{pmatrix}\).

Multiply every element of the matrix by 4.

\(4A = \begin{pmatrix} 32 & -4 \\ 16 & 28 \end{pmatrix}\)

text: Find the value of \(x\) for which the matrix \(\begin{pmatrix} x & 4 \\ 6 & 4 \end{pmatrix}\) has no inverse.
explanation:
A matrix has no inverse when its determinant is zero.

\(\det = (x)(4) - (4)(6) = 4x - 24\)

Setting \(4x - 24 = 0\): \(x = \frac{24}{4} = 6\)

Multiply every element of the matrix by -1.

\(-1A = \begin{pmatrix} -3 & -8 \\ -2 & -5 \end{pmatrix}\)

Add the matrices element by element.

Top row: \(1 + (3) = 4\), \(1 + (5) = 6\)

Bottom row: \(1 + (-2) = -1\), \(1 + (1) = 2\)

So \(A + B = \begin{pmatrix} 4 & 6 \\ -1 & 2 \end{pmatrix}\).
